summary: Doi Hua Mu is the viewpoint destination on Doi Pui’s signed summit nature trail in Doi Suthep–Pui National Park. The easiest described option is a forest walk from Doi Pui summit to the viewpoint and back, with interpretation panels, changing highland forest and a Chiang Mai outlook. It is a real hike rather than a roadside viewpoint, and access and conditions should be checked with the park before setting out.
whyGo: Get a half-day forest walk and a city panorama within reach of Chiang Mai.
Learn about local plants, insects and the forest’s history from trail interpretation panels.
Choose a route presented as manageable for beginner hikers, with wooden steps on steeper sections.
bestFor: Visitors wanting a nature outing without travelling to a distant national park
Beginner hikers comfortable walking around five kilometres over uneven ground
Birdwatchers and people interested in the ecology of Doi Suthep–Pui
skipIf: You need step-free access or a reliably easy paved path.
You are not prepared to arrange mountain transport and confirm the trail is open.
You want a guaranteed clear view, cherry blossoms or a guided hike.
duration: Allow about 3.5 hours for the 4.9 km return Doi Pui summit–Doi Hua Mu route, according to the trail feature; this is walking time and does not include Chiang Mai transfers or long stops. Other nearby routes have different lengths and difficulty.
cost: A Chiang Mai hiking group’s February 2026 outing notice says park admission at the Doi Pui campground was ฿100 for foreign visitors and ฿20 for Thai visitors, cash only. Child rates and whether the same charge will apply at each trailhead in December 2026 were not confirmed. Transport is extra.
hours: A recent trail feature lists daily opening from 08:00 to 16:00 and gives the park number as 053-210-244. Confirm current hours, trail access and any seasonal closure before travelling; do not plan a late start.
bestTime: Start in the morning to leave time for the return walk and enjoy cooler conditions. December is the cool season, but mist and viewpoint visibility vary. The separate longer route toward Khun Chang Khian may coincide with wild Himalayan cherry flowering from late December into February; blooms are not guaranteed and this is not the same as the short return route.
gettingThere: The Doi Pui summit trail begins in the park’s upper mountain area, reached by road via Doi Suthep and Bhubing Palace toward the Doi Pui campground. A private driver is simplest; local red songthaews can be hired from the Doi Suthep approach, with fares depending on group size, waiting and return arrangements. Agree pickup and return in advance. The road is steep and narrow; the trail feature advises against low-clearance small cars and inexperienced mountain drivers.
booking: No day-hike reservation process was verified. Contact Doi Suthep–Pui National Park at 053-210-244 to confirm trail status and any admission requirement. Camping is a separate activity and requires advance arrangements.
accessibility: No step-free or wheelchair access information was found. The route includes uneven forest ground and wooden-log steps on steeper sections, so it is unsuitable for wheelchair users and may be difficult for visitors with limited balance or mobility. Toilets and accessible facilities at the actual trailhead were not verified.
practicalTips: Check the trail map at the start and stay on the marked route; the park has several trailheads and route options.
Wear shoes with good grip, carry water and bring a light layer, sun protection and rain cover.
Keep cash for park entry and transport; confirm the 2026 tariff and exact collection point before going.
Allow daylight for the return and arrange a definite pickup rather than relying on finding a ride at the summit.
Carry out rubbish and keep noise low for wildlife and other walkers.
decemberNotes: The cool season makes the highland walk appealing, but mornings can be cold and mist can obscure the Doi Hua Mu view. The longer route connecting Doi Hua Mu with Khun Chang Khian is associated with wild Himalayan cherry viewing, generally late December to February; exact timing varies by year. December and New Year are busy travel weeks, so confirm access and transport early. No specific December 2026 closure or event was verified.
uncertainties: The published route description and 08:00–16:00 hours are from a recent feature, not a live park status notice; current openings may change.
The 2026 Doi Pui fee was reported by a local hiking group; child rates and exact collection arrangements for this trail remain unclear.
No reliable fare or timetable for public songthaew service to the Doi Pui trailhead was found.
Step-free access, toilets, guide availability and trail condition in December 2026 are unverified.
